For Personal Financial Management of Parents and Young Professionals
in San Fernando City, La Union
Brix A. Directo  ·  Cyrille John M. Rubis  ·  Djaunathan Albert S. Madayag
Lead Developer             UI/UX & Documentation             Project Manager & QA
Adviser: Ms. Ellen F. Mangaoang, DIT   ·   Lorma Colleges CCSE   ·   November 9, 2026
The Problem: Filipino Finance Management Gaps
Filipino users abandon expense trackers — GCash, Shopee, and multi-wallet transactions require too much manual effort.
Existing apps don't understand Taglish, GCash, Paluwagan, ShopeePay, or local merchant names.
Apps show charts but create no consequences when spending warnings are ignored. Users need nudges, not just graphs.
BSP CFIS 2025  ·  BSP Consumer Expectations Survey
What This Study Aims to Do
Assess existing financial management practices, budgeting challenges, and expense tracking behaviors of parents (35–55) and young professionals (21–35) in San Fernando City, La Union
Design and develop SmartSpend — an offline-first Flutter/Android application with Taglish AI, multi-modal input, and a transaction-derived Financial Health Score
Evaluate the system using the System Usability Scale (SUS, N=30), targeting a mean score ≥80 ("Good" per Bangor, Kortum & Miller, 2009)
No existing study evaluates an integrated mobile prototype combining Taglish AI logging + GCash screenshot import + transaction-derived Financial Health Score for the Filipino context.
Choice architecture guides behavior without restricting freedom. Budget alerts, Warning Decay (−5 pts/day), and startup gap prompts are designed nudges applied at the moment of decision.
36 badges + streaks = Competence reward. Customizable goals = Autonomy. Filipino-first Taglish framing = Relatedness. SDT explains why the gamification sustains habit formation.
Losses feel ~2× more painful than equivalent gains. Warning Decay: FHS drops −5 pts/day when budget warnings are ignored — making the cost of ignoring alerts concrete and visible.

The Financial Health Score adapts the CBA–Melbourne Institute Observed Financial Health Indicator (Comerton-Forde et al., 2018) — a transaction-based 0–100 scale with equal-weighted components. We call ours a "Prototype Observed Financial Health Indicator (FHI)" per Melbourne Institute naming guidance. UNSGSA (2021) validates using transaction data as an early-stage complement to survey-based scales.
The FHS Formula — Where It Came From

FHS (Full Mode) = 4 × 25 pts each:

① Savings Rate    = 25 × min(1, rate/0.20)
② Overspend Ctrl  = 25 × (1−weighted/active)
③ Budget Adher.   = 25 × (onBudget/total)
④ Log Consistency = 25 × (loggedDays/active)

Adj: Warning Decay −5 pts/day (max −15)
Lightweight: Spending Restraint + Category
Balance + Consistency + Habit Streak
⏳  📋 Final data — N=30 respondents (Oct–Nov 2026). Survey collection complete: 96.7% AI intent (29/30), 93.3% GCash usage (28/30).
Meet Peso — Your AI Money Buddy
Idle animation (bob + eye blink every ~4s), mood pop-in elastic transition. Responds to FHS score, budget status, and user gestures.
PesoVoiceService: 2–4 random Taglish variants per context. Prevents semantic satiation — different line every session.
Double-tap → surprised + voice line. Long-press → context tip sheet. Idle 8s → winks at you (once/hour anti-Clippy).
🟢 Green ≥70 · 🟠 Orange ≥50 · 🔴 Red <50. Score tier visible instantly without reading the number.
Log daily → streak celebration → reinforces habit. FHS tier change → Peso reacts. Notification tap → context greeting.
These are design features grounded in SDT and Nudge Theory. Longitudinal behavioral effect has NOT been measured — present as design, not as measured outcome.

On-device regex redacts BEFORE sending:
• PH mobile numbers (09XX/+63)
• GCash ref numbers (12–18 digits)
• OTPs and PIN codes
• Bank account numbers

Note: Free-tier Gemini content may be used to improve Google products.

User connects Ollama/LM Studio/Jan on their own PC. While server is reachable, no data leaves the home network.

Local-only toggle: AI stops responding instead of falling back to cloud — for maximum privacy.

Gemma 4 E2B (~2.6 GB) via LiteRT LM SDK. Viable on 6 GB RAM / Android 10+ phones.

Status: Planned ~2027. Listed as Recommendation, NOT a delivered feature.

text_content: AN AI-ASSISTED MOBILE FINANCIAL TRACKING AND ADVISORY APPLICATION FOR PERSONAL FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT

MEMBERS:

Brix A. Directo
Cyrille John M. Rubis
Djaunathan Albert S. Madayag
Adviser: Mr. Johnny Flores Verzola, MTS

Project Context & The Problem
Gap of the Study
What is SmartSpend?
Conceptual Framework (IPO Model)
Statements of Objectives
Scope and Limitations
Purpose, Description & Beneficiaries
Technical Background
Review of Related Literature & Systems

Research Design
Population and Locale
Ethical Considerations
Data Gathering Tools & Procedures
Software Methodology (Agile Kanban)

In today’s digital era, financial management has become increasingly important, especially for young professionals who need to monitor their expenses and manage their budgets effectively. While many mobile applications exist, most still rely heavily on manual input and lack intelligent features that help users understand their financial behavior.

Traditional financial tracking systems act as passive tools where users manually record expenses and review static summaries. Because of this, users often find expense tracking tedious, leading to inconsistent usage and incomplete records.

With the advancement of Artificial Intelligence, especially Large Language Models, mobile applications can now interpret natural language and provide smarter, more interactive financial assistance.

Only 2% of Filipino adults correctly answered all basic financial literacy questions (BSP, 2021)

Only 46% of Filipinos maintain any household budget (BSP, 2021)

Only 7% have attended any financial literacy training (BSP, 2021)

Many households spend beyond monthly income food, transport, utilities outpace savings (PSA FIES, 2021)

Most Filipinos do not use structured financial tools citing: manual effort, poor local language support, lack of feedback (BSP, 2021)

Parents (35–55) primary household financial decision-makers, yet among the lowest in formal financial account ownership and structured budgeting (BSP, 2021)

Young Professionals (21–35) managing independent income but often without financial literacy training or tools 

Flores (2025) Filipino workers show "come-what-may" attitudes, high debt dependence, reliance on traditional saving methods 

Filipino workers show "come-what-may" attitudes, high debt dependence, reliance on traditional saving methods

SmartSpend AI-powered mobile financial assistant for Android

Not just an expense recorder a financial companion

Key capabilities: Natural language expense input (Filipino-English), Conversational AI (Q&A, prices, guidance), Financial Health Score (0–100), Voice + OCR + barcode + manual input, Offline + cloud sync

General: Design, develop, and evaluate SmartSpend for parents (35–55) and young professionals (21–35) in La Union

Objective 1: Assess the existing financial management practices, common budgeting challenges, and expense tracking behaviors of the target population through structured surveys and interviews

Objective 2: Design and develop the SmartSpend mobile application — including LLM API integration via context injection architecture, selected through comparative benchmarking

Objective 3: Evaluate the usability of SmartSpend using the System Usability Scale (SUS)

Android only
offline + cloud
Filipino-English AI
Voice + OCR + barcode + manual

OCR depends on receipt image quality
AI requires internet connection
No bank integration (no open-banking APIs in PH)
No professional financial or tax advice
Market price estimates may not be real-time
AI key: 60 requests/day cap for security
AI does NOT transmit names, account numbers, or personal data to external API

Parents (35–55) - automated tracking, FHS, multi-period summaries; significant financial responsibility with limited access to formal tools
Budget-conscious individuals - expense control, AI-driven analysis, wallet balances (GCash, Maya, banks)
Technology enthusiasts - experience AI + LLM in a practical app
Demo/Evaluation users - Demo Mode, no registration needed
Note: SmartSpend is a financial companion - NOT a professional financial advisor

Flutter: Android UI framework (Google)
SQLite via sqflite: local offline database (14 categories, 9 payment methods)
Firebase Firestore: cloud sync | Firebase Auth - secure login | Firebase Crashlytics - crash reporting
LLM API: AI engine (selected via comparative benchmarking: free-tier, fast, Filipino-English capable, modular architecture)
Google ML Kit: OCR (smart routing: single item → AI chat; 3+ items → import review screen)
speech_to_text: voice input (en-PH) | mobile_scanner - barcode | System share sheet - JSON backup/restore
fl_chart: analytics charts | local_auth - biometric login
Financial Health Score (FHS): 4-component formula, 0–100 (full details in Chapter 3)

Technical Benchmarking (Objective 2 tool) — Full results in Chapter 3 

Evaluated multiple candidate LLM APIs based on:

Inference speed (response latency)
Filipino-English accuracy
Context window capacity
Cost feasibility (free-tier for academic deployment)
Selected model: best balance of speed, accuracy, and cost Architecture is modular — AI engine can be swapped without rebuilding the entire system

Think of it as: a grade for your financial habits — not a credit score
4 components × 25% each:
Savings Rate — are you saving 20% of income? (based on 50/30/20 rule)
Overspend Control — how many days did you exceed your budget?
Budget Adherence — what % of budget categories stayed within limits?
Logging Consistency — are you recording expenses regularly?
Score = 25% × each component | Bounded: min 0, max 100
Consequence System (decay): Day 1 warning ignored → gentle nudge −5pts | Day 2 → stronger warning −5pts | Day 3 → critical alert −5pts | Minimum: 0
Basis: UNSGSA Framework (2021) on measuring financial health

SmartSpend AI — 6 roles:
Expense parsing — "paid 150 for groceries" → auto-recorded
Proactive insights — alerts when spending is unusual or budget nearly exceeded
General financial Q&A — banking products, SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG
Market price estimates — "magkano ang second-hand iPhone 13?"
Buying & selling advice — "is this a good deal for my situation?"
Financial planning — "how do I split my ₱18,000 salary?"
Privacy: Only anonymized descriptions → API. No names, no account numbers, no personal data.
Efficiency: Conversation summarization — compressed summary replaces full chat history in API calls

Mixed methods: qualitative (interviews) + quantitative (surveys + SUS)
Descriptive-developmental: design, build, and evaluate a functional system
SUS — System Usability Scale:
Developed by Brooke (1996), validated Bangor et al. (2009)
10 standard questions, answered after using the system
Score: 0–100 | 80+ = Good ← our target
Administered to all 30 respondents after live demo

Location: San Fernando City, La Union
Respondents (n=30): Parents 35–55 (n=20) + Young Professionals 21–35 (n=10)
Sampling: Purposive — intentionally selecting individuals with financial management experience
Validators:
Survey Content Validator: Susan C. Arquisal — BS Commerce (Management), Active Business Owner
SUS Process Reviewer: Benjie G. Bucasas — BS IT cum laude, IT Team Lead

Agile Kanban — flexible, visual task management for software development
Tasks move across a board: Backlog → Requirements → Design → Development → Testing → Deployment → Done/Review
Phases can overlap or repeat — unlike rigid sequential models
WIP limits prevent overload and maintain focus

VOLUNTARY PARTICIPATION | INFORMED CONSENT | FULL CONFIDENTIALITY | ACADEMIC USE ONLY
OBJECTIVE 1: SURVEY (VALIDATED: SUSAN ARQUISAL) + INTERVIEWS
OBJECTIVE 2: NO INSTRUMENT — DEVELOPMENT PHASE + LLM TECHNICAL BENCHMARKING
OBJECTIVE 3: SUS QUESTIONNAIRE (PROCESS REVIEWED: BENJIE BUCASAS) + ADDITIONAL FEEDBACK

Problem: Only 2% full financial literacy (BSP 2021); parents are primary decision-makers but underserved; Filipino households overspend
Gap: No app combines Filipino-English AI + offline + FHS + no bank integration needed
Solution: SmartSpend — AI-assisted, offline, multi-modal, full financial companion
Target: Parents (35–55) + Young Professionals (21–35), La Union, n=30
Key innovations: FHS (0–100, 4 components) + Expanded AI (6 roles) + Consequence System + Conversation Summarization
Method: Mixed methods + Agile Kanban + LLM comparative benchmarking + SUS (target: 80+)
Validators: Susan C. Arquisal (survey) | Benjie G. Bucasas (SUS process)
WE WELCOME YOUR QUESTIONS AND FEEDBACK AFTER THE DEMO VIDEO.

numerical_data.slide_21_sus:
Problem: Only 2% full financial literacy (BSP 2021); parents are primary decision-makers but underserved; Filipino households overspend
Gap: No app combines Filipino-English AI + offline + FHS + no bank integration needed
Solution: SmartSpend — AI-assisted, offline, multi-modal, full financial companion
Target: Parents (35–55) + Young Professionals (21–35), La Union, n=30
Key innovations: FHS (0–100, 4 components) + Expanded AI (6 roles) + Consequence System + Conversation Summarization
Method: Mixed methods + Agile Kanban + LLM comparative benchmarking + SUS (target: 80+)
Validators: Susan C. Arquisal (survey) | Benjie G. Bucasas (SUS process)
